It is early March.[^1] [^2]

[^1]: Most likely, Monday, 3 March 1969. Since March 1st, the designated school start date, was a Saturday that year

[^2]: We moved to US on April 1974. I had just started 6th grade. Working backwards, is how we arrived at this date

Gathered in the school grounds are some of the 1,034,000 children born during the Baby Boom era in Korea.

There are as many parents, nearly all are mothers, gathered by 반 or class.

My mom is seen wearing a dark traditional 두루마기[^3] [^4] along with a light colored western shawl. Completing her outfit is a 고무신

[^3]: The Durumagi (두루마기) is a traditional Korean overcoat worn as the outermost layer of the Hanbok. Its name literally translates to "closed all around," which refers to its most defining feature: unlike other traditional coats, it has no side or back slits.(https://namu.wiki/w/%EB%91%90%EB%A3%A8%EB%A7%88%EA%B8%B0)

[^4]: Interestingly, the word for scroll is 두루마리, I used to confuse these 2 words

By this time, my father had been in Vietnam for more than 2 years.

Earning pay that would finally get my parents out of debt and allow them to move to a fast growing town of 주안 from 부평.

My mother is perhaps hearkening back to her childhood.

When her mother was known for combining both traditional and western wear as the leading lady in town.

Although I was one of many, hundreds that day at 주안국민 (초등) 학교, I felt special, I felt I could do almost anything, because my mother was there with me and my father was backing me up financially from a far.
